q2.answer: In the bone of the upper jaw/gum, next to the front teeth (the alveolar cleft).
q2.where: Sheet 1, key message box and 'What this model shows'

q3.answer: The small tooth next to the front tooth (lateral incisor) on the left. About half of children with a cleft don't have this tooth on the cleft side.

q4.answer: It needs bone to grow/come down into. The graft gives it bone.
q4.where: Sheet 1, 'The eye tooth' and 'Why surgeons do the bone graft'

q5.answer: About 8 to 11 years old, chosen by how far the teeth have grown, before the eye tooth comes through.

q7.answer: New bone fills the gap and the gum has healed over it. The eye tooth is a little lower.
q7.where: Sheet 2, key message box and 'What has changed'

q8.answer: With an X-ray at about 3 to 6 months after surgery.

q9.answer: Your hip can be sore for a while.

q10.answer: It has come down through the new bone and is fully in the row of teeth.

q11.where: Sheet 3, key message box and 'What has changed'

q12.answer: Two plans: close the space (braces move the eye tooth into the gap, reshaped and filled to look like the missing tooth), or keep the space (a removable plate with a false tooth while growing, later an implant or a bridge with one wing). The cleft team will talk it through with you.
